arxiv-2012-06137.title: Saving superconducting quantum processors from qubit decay and correlated errors generated by gamma and cosmic rays
arxiv-2012-06137.creator: John M. Martinis
arxiv-2012-06137.description: A 2020 arXiv research paper by John M. Martinis. Error-corrected quantum computers can only work if errors are small and uncorrelated. Here I show how cosmic rays or stray background radiation affects superconducting qubits by modeling the phonon to electron/quasiparticle down-conversion physics. For present designs, the model predicts about 57% of the radiation energy breaks Cooper pairs into quasiparticles, which then vigorously suppress the qubit energy relaxation time ( T 1 ∼ 600 T_{1}\sim 600\, ns) over a large area (cm) and for a long time (ms).

arxiv-2106-06179.title: A physics-inspired alternative to spatial filtering for large-eddy simulations of turbulent flows
arxiv-2106-06179.creator: Perry L. Johnson
arxiv-2106-06179.description: Abstract Large-eddy simulations (LES) are widely-used for computing high Reynolds number turbulent flows. Spatial filtering theory for LES is not without its shortcomings, including how to define filtering for wall-bounded flows, commutation errors for non-uniform filters, and extensibility to flows with additional complexity, such as multiphase flows.

arxiv-2203-00597.title: Path sampling of recurrent neural networks by incorporating known physics
arxiv-2203-00597.creator: Sun-Ting Tsai, Eric Fields, Yijia Xu, En-Jui Kuo, Pratyush Tiwary*
arxiv-2203-00597.description: Abstract Recurrent neural networks have seen widespread use in modeling dynamical systems in varied domains such as weather prediction, text prediction and several others. Often one wishes to supplement the experimentally observed dynamics with prior knowledge or intuition about the system.

arxiv-2305-04781.title: An extension of Schur’s irreducibility result
arxiv-2305-04781.creator: ANKITA JINDAL AND SUDESH KAUR KHANDUJA (Dedicated to Professor André Leroy on his 65 t ​ h 65^{th} birthday)
arxiv-2305-04781.description: Abstract Abstract Let n\geq 2 be an integer. Let \phi(x) belonging to \mbox{$\mathbb{Z}$}[x] be a monic polynomial which is irreducible modulo all primes less than or equal to n . Let a_{0}(x),a_{1}(x),\dots,a_{n-1}(x) belonging to \mbox{$\mathbb{Z}$}[x] be polynomials each having degree less than \deg\phi(x) and a_{n} be an integer. Assume that a_{n} and the content of a_{0}(x) are coprime with n!

arxiv-2306-04669.title: Spectral variability of photospheric radiation due to faculae II: Facular contrasts for cool main-sequence stars. 2023 Spectral variability of photospheric radiation due to faculae II: Facular contrasts for cool main-sequence stars. –
arxiv-2306-04669.creator: Charlotte M. Norris, Yvonne C. Unruh, Veronika Witzke, Sami K. Solanki, Natalie A. Krivova, Alexander I. Shapiro, Kok Leng Yeo, Robert Cameron, Benjamin Beeck
arxiv-2306-04669.description: Abstract Magnetic features on the surface of stars, such as spots and faculae, cause stellar spectral variability on time-scales of days and longer. For stars other than the Sun, the spectral signatures of faculae are poorly understood, limiting our ability to account for stellar pollution in exoplanet transit observations.

arxiv-2307-05700.title: SepHRNet: Generating High-Resolution Crop Maps from Remote Sensing imagery using HRNet with Separable Convolution
arxiv-2307-05700.creator: Priyanka Goyal, Sohan Patnaik, Adway Mitra, Manjira Sinha
arxiv-2307-05700.description: Abstract The accurate mapping of crop production is crucial for ensuring food security, effective resource management, and sustainable agricultural practices. One way to achieve this is by analyzing high-resolution satellite imagery. Deep Learning has been successful in analyzing images, including remote sensing imagery. However, capturing intricate crop patterns is challenging due to their complexity and variability.

arxiv-2402-03010.title: Homotopy equivalences and Grothendieck duality over rings with finite Gorenstein weak global dimension
arxiv-2402-03010.description: Abstract Abstract: Let R be a ring with Gwgldim (R)<\infty . We obtain a triangle-equivalence \mbox{\rm K}(R\text{-}\mbox{\rm GProj})\simeq\mbox{\rm K}(R\text{-}\mbox{\rm GInj}) which restricts to a triangle-equivalence \mbox{\rm K}(R\text{-}\mbox{\rm Proj}) \simeq\mbox{\rm K}(R\text{-}\mbox{\rm Inj}) . This class of rings includes, among others, (left) Gorenstein rings, Ding-Chen rings and the more general Gorenstein n -coherent rings ( n\in\mathbb{N}\cup\{\infty\},n\geq 2 ).

arxiv-2409-17993.title: SSHNet: Unsupervised Cross-modal Homography Estimation via Problem Reformulation and Split Optimization
arxiv-2409-17993.creator: Junchen Yu, Si-Yuan Cao, Runmin Zhang, Chenghao Zhang, Zhu Yu, Shujie Chen, Bailin Yang, Hui-Liang Shen
arxiv-2409-17993.description: Abstract We propose a novel unsupervised cross-modal homography estimation learning framework, named S plit S upervised H omography estimation N etwork (SSHNet). SSHNet reformulates the unsupervised cross-modal homography estimation into two supervised sub-problems, each addressed by its specialized network: a homography estimation network and a modality transfer network.

arxiv-2503-14977.title: Enhancement of Large Eddy Simulation for the prediction of an intake flow rig using sequential Data Assimilation
arxiv-2503-14977.creator: Lucas Villanueva, Karine Truffin, Jacques Borée, Marcello Meldi, Institut Pprime, CNRS - ISAE-ENSMA - Université de Poitiers,11 Bd. Marie et Pierre Curie, Site du Futuroscope, TSA 41123, 86073 Poitiers Cedex 9, France, Institut Carnot IFPEN Transports Energie, IFP Energies nouvelles,1-4 avenue de Bo
arxiv-2503-14977.description: Abstract A Data Assimilation (DA) strategy based on an ensemble Kalman filter (EnKF) is used to enhance the predictive capabilities of scale resolving numerical tools for the analysis of flows exhibiting cyclic behaviour. More precisely, an ensemble of numerical runs using Large Eddy Simulation (LES) for the compressible steady-state flow rig is augmented via the integration of high-fidelity data.

arxiv-2506-01444.title: Variance-Based Defense Against Blended Backdoor Attacks Thanks: This paper has been accepted at ECML PKDD 2025.
arxiv-2506-01444.creator: Sujeevan Aseervatham (✉), Achraf Kerzazi, Younès Bennani
arxiv-2506-01444.description: Abstract Backdoor attacks represent a subtle yet effective class of cyberattacks targeting AI models, primarily due to their stealthy nature. The model behaves normally on clean data but exhibits malicious behavior only when the attacker embeds a specific trigger into the input.

arxiv-2508-07949.title: Algebraic approach to a d d -dimensional matrix Hamiltonian with so( OPEN d + 1 ) d+1) symmetry
arxiv-2508-07949.creator: C. Quesne
arxiv-2508-07949.description: Abstract A novel spin-extended so( d + 1 d+1 ,1) algebra is introduced and shown to provide an interesting framework for discussing the properties of a d d -dimensional matrix Hamiltonian with spin 1/2 and so( d + 1 d+1 ) symmetry.

arxiv-2509-09476.title: Bath-induced stabilization of classical non-linear response in two dimensional infrared spectroscopy
arxiv-2509-09476.creator: Rajesh Dutta, Mike Reppert
arxiv-2509-09476.description: Abstract Classical response functions have shown considerable promise in computational 2D IR modeling; however, a simple diagrammatic description, analogous to that for open quantum systems, has been lacking. While a promising diagrammatic approach has recently been introduced for isolated systems, the resulting nonlinear response functions remain unstable at long times, a characteristic feature of integrable classical systems.

pmc-10670041.title: Experimental Predictions for Norm-Conserving Spontaneous Collapse
pmc-10670041.creator: D. W. Snoke, D. N. Maienshein
pmc-10670041.description: Previous work has shown that nonlocal collapse in quantum mechanics can be described by a deterministic, non-unitary operator added to the standard Schrödinger equation. In terms of key aspects, this term differs from prior work on spontaneous collapse. In this paper, we discuss the possible predictions of this model that can be tested by experiments.

pmc-11354852.title: Mineralocorticoid Receptor Signaling in Peripheral Blood Cells in Patients with Multiple Sclerosis
pmc-11354852.creator: Franziska Küstermann, Kathy Busse, Johannes Orthgieß, Muriel Stoppe, Sarah Haars, Florian Then Bergh
pmc-11354852.description: Multiple sclerosis (MS) is associated with alterations in neuroendocrine function, primarily the hypothalamic–pituitary–adrenal axis, including lower expression of the glucocorticoid receptor (GR) and its target genes in peripheral blood mononuclear cells (PBMC) or full blood. We previously found reduced mineralocorticoid receptor (MR) expression in MS patients’ peripheral blood.

pmc-12968515.title: Resource Availability Modulates Gene Expression Across Life Stages in a Migratory Butterfly
pmc-12968515.creator: D Shipilina, L Höök, K Näsvall, V Talla, A Palahí, E Parkes, R Vila, G Talavera, N Backström
pmc-12968515.description: Natural populations are in constant need of balancing resource allocation to compensate for seasonal environmental variation. In many insects, a well‐established trade‐off between migration and reproduction exists. While this trade‐off has been characterised phenotypically for decades, the underlying regulatory pathways are poorly understood.

pmc-12988658.title: A Summary of the Evidence for Managing Exercise Phobia in Patients After Anterior Cruciate Ligament Reconstruction Surgery
pmc-12988658.creator: Xuemei Zheng, Chunqiu He, Wenling Tian, Mengjing Chang, Xiangyue Liu, Dongfa Liao, Lin Cui
pmc-12988658.description: BackgroundIn recent years, the incidence of anterior cruciate ligament (ACL) injuries has risen persistently. Notably, some patients develop movement fear after ACL reconstruction surgery. This psychological issue significantly reduces patients’ exercise rehabilitation adherence and active participation willingness. It also exacerbates family caregiving pressures and healthcare systems’ socioeconomic burden.

pmc-13045211.title: Identification of Blood Pressure‐Associated Metabolites by Integrating Metabolomic and Genetic Analysis
pmc-13045211.creator: Yuanjiao Liu, Chunxiao Cheng, Xiong‐Fei Pan, Wei Shao, Dan Zhou, Yimin Zhu
pmc-13045211.description: This study aimed to identify blood pressure‐associated metabolites and explore their underlying pathways using multiomics data from 1188 Chinese participants. Serum metabolite levels were profiled using untargeted and widely targeted metabolomic technologies. The associations of metabolites as well as ratios with blood pressure were assessed using generalized linear models (GLM). Targeted metabolomics was used to replicate a subset of metabolites.

pmc-13054774.title: Psychological Factors Are Associated With Lower Limb Kinematics During Uphill Walking and Running in Women With Patellofemoral Pain
pmc-13054774.creator: Isabela Regina dos Reis, Ana Caroline Brites de Magistris Martins, Beatriz Paiva Soares, Jamilly Radiuc Cipolli, Deborah Hebling Spinoso
pmc-13054774.description: Background and PurposePatellofemoral pain (PFP) is a common condition in women and is associated with high recurrence rates. Kinematic alterations are among the factors that may persist even after muscle strengthening programs. Given the multifactorial nature of PFP, non‐mechanical factors, such as kinesiophobia, may be related to the movement patterns adopted by this population.
